Question: Through the use of theorems on logarithms, \(\log\dfrac ab+\log\dfrac bc+\log\dfrac cd-\log\dfrac{ay}{dx}\) can be reduced to:
Solution:
Adding logarithms multiplies their arguments, which lets the intermediate factors cancel. All logarithms have the same base, positive and different from \(1\), and every original argument must be positive. These conditions also make all six variables nonzero.

First combine the three added logarithms:
\[
\log\frac ab+\log\frac bc+\log\frac cd
=\log\left(\frac ab\cdot\frac bc\cdot\frac cd\right)
=\log\frac ad.
\]
Subtracting a logarithm divides its argument, so the full expression becomes
\[
\log\left(\frac{a/d}{ay/(dx)}\right)
=\log\left(\frac ad\cdot\frac{dx}{ay}\right)
=\log\frac xy.
\]
The quotient of the two positive arguments is positive, so the final logarithm is defined. The answer is \(\log\dfrac xy\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
